summary: Michigan light (1869) on the Straits of Mackinac, discontinued in 1906, sold in 1913, and owned by Emmet County since 2008. Open for summer tours.

access.note: Owned by Emmet County; open for tours in summer (mid-May to mid-October, $3 admission).

events.note: Congress appropriated $20,000 for the station (26 July per county; 28 July per LighthouseFriends).
Brick dwelling with attached tower built in 1869.
Wooden steamer Waldo A. Avery caught fire in the Straits and was run toward the light (county account, following Pepper).
Discontinuance authorized 12 November 1906; last exhibited 15 December 1906.
Board approved an auction sale (22 May 1907); the top bid of $875 was rejected.
Sold to Sam Smith for $1,425 on 30 July 1913 (county); LighthouseFriends describes an auction.
Emmet County bought the property for $710,000.
Reopened to the public with a gala celebration on 30 May 2009.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Board authorized discontinuance on 12 November 1906 and the light was last exhibited at the close of navigation on 15 December 1906; both dates are consistent.

LighthouseFriends dates the Old Mackinac Point fog signal to 5 November 1890 and the light's funding to 1891; the county history dates the Old Mackinac Point station to 1892. The fog signal came first.

notes_for_editor: Unresolved: (1) first keeper: the archive roster lists Gabriel Allotte for 1869 alone, while LighthouseFriends and the county history name Charles Louisignau (1869-1875) as first keeper; the story says so. (2) Start of construction: 1868 (LighthouseFriends) vs early 1869 (county); the story says so. (3) Focal height: 102 ft (LighthouseFriends, county-derived Pepper table) vs record's 33.0 m; the tower height is 38 ft in the archive and 'about forty feet' in LighthouseFriends. (4) Lens: the archive gives 1892 for the original lens; the county history describes the 1869 lantern with a third-and-a-half order lens; not resolved. (5) Light status: archive says no active aid, private aid yes; the county says it reopened in 2009; the record's 'active' needs a human check; no current Coast Guard list read. (6) The 1893 Avery rescue (skiff, seventeen crew, steering toward the light) rests on the county history and Pepper's Beacon article; the Grand Rapids item only confirms the burning and the cargo sale. No other contemporary report was located. (7) Davenport's weekly ice letters are quoted from the county history, which quotes Pepper; the letters themselves were not read. (8) Pepper's article and the county page are second-hand for the National Archives letters. (9) The Wikipedia article was used only for leads (a 2019 cottage stay, a 2009 relighting, a 2009 relighting ceremony with senators, and the NOAA chart listing); none of those facts is in the story. (10) The Lighthouse Board repair entries were matched by station name in the OCR text; the scan pages are the corpus's, and the printed page numbers were not confirmed against the page images. (11) Emmet's 'approximately 10 acres' vs LighthouseFriends's 11.5 acres: the story uses 'about ten acres'. (12) Newspapers: one Chronicling America search for 'McGulpin Point' in Michigan papers, 1869-1915, returned no hits; a search for the Avery fire returned the Grand Rapids item and others (not read). (13) Page citations are scan pages for the Lighthouse Board volumes (printed page numbers not confirmed).
